hook.text: A 3D digital twin of the building — every beam, pipe, and duct — built before construction starts.

buildup.text: BIM combines architecture, structure, and MEP in one model — clashes are detected digitally.

discovery.text: A pipe running through a beam is caught on screen — not on site where fixing costs 10x more.

twist.text: 4D BIM adds time — linking the model to the schedule. 5D adds cost — quantity takeoffs are automatic.

climax.text: The Shanghai Tower used BIM to coordinate 100+ subcontractors — reducing rework by 30%.

punchline.text: Build it twice — once digitally to find problems, once physically to avoid them.

quiz.question: What is the primary benefit of BIM clash detection?
options: It makes the building look better in 3D renderings
Conflicts between systems are found digitally before construction, when fixes are cheap
It allows clients to choose interior paint colors in advance

details.summary: Building Information Modeling creates a digital 3D model containing all physical and functional information about a facility. BIM enables clash detection between trades before construction, quantity extraction for estimating, 4D schedule simulation, and facility management after handover.
details.whyItMatters: BIM reduces errors, rework, and waste by detecting conflicts in the digital model instead of discovering them during construction when changes cost 10 to 100 times more to fix.
takeaways: 3D clash detection identifies conflicts between structural, mechanical, and electrical systems
4D BIM links the model to the schedule for visual construction sequence simulation
5D BIM integrates cost data for real-time budget tracking as design evolves

faq.question: How does BIM clash detection work?
faq.answer: Each discipline, structural, mechanical, electrical, and plumbing, creates its model. Software overlays all models and automatically identifies locations where elements from different disciplines occupy the same space, such as a duct running through a beam.

faq.question: What is the return on investment for implementing BIM on construction projects?
faq.answer: Studies report BIM ROI of 300 to 500% through reduced rework, fewer change orders, faster construction, and better coordination. A Stanford study found BIM eliminates up to 40% of unbudgeted changes. The investment in modeling is small compared to the cost of clashes discovered during construction.
